result:
**Key criterion.** Ana fails to distinguish primes p ≠ q exactly when some value vector v on S = {x₁,…,xₙ} is compatible with both a nonconstant p-periodic and a nonconstant q-periodic function. Let G be the bipartite graph whose vertices are the residues mod p and mod q hit by S, with one edge per x ∈ S. Ana wins for the pair (p,q) iff G is connected and S covers all residues mod p or all residues mod q. The covering condition holds because a constant v is only ruled out for a prime whose residues S fully covers.

**Lower bound.** At most one prime below 100 can be "not fully covered," since any two such primes give Ana a losing pair. If 97 is the exceptional prime, then 89 and 83 must both be fully covered, and connectivity of the (83, 89) graph needs at least 83 + 89 − 1 = 171 elements. Other choices of the exceptional prime force n ≥ 179 or n ≥ 185. So n ≥ 171.

**Upper bound.** I did not verify a construction with n = 171 in full. The sketch is to take S as a spanning tree of K₈₃,₈₉ lifted via CRT, with every element congruent to the same residue mod 97. That handles all pairs involving 97, and the remaining pairs among primes ≤ 89 can plausibly be handled by choosing the other residues appropriately. I have not confirmed this, so the exact answer is not established here.

**Verdicts.**
- Solution 1 (185) uses the wrong lower-bound reasoning. It assumes every pair needs p + q − 1 elements, but the pair involving 97 does not need full coverage, which allows n = 171.
- Solution 2 (98) is too small. The lower bound above gives at least 171.
- Solution 3 (186) is an unsupported upper-bound argument. Its claim that the interval {0,…,185} works is not justified, and its lower-bound sketch is incomplete. The lower bound is 171, not 186.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
